fact: The Minister of Security, presenting his department's results for 2022-2026 on 2 October 2026, listed the dematerialisation of certain working tools, notably the main courante (occurrence book) and SYGESS, among what has been achieved; the report gives no count of stations using it and does not say how the entry is made.

The dematerialisation of the main courante is presented by the Minister of Security on 2 October 2026 as an achievement of the Ministry of Security itself over 2022-2026; no partner, vendor or source of finance is named.

In late December 2023 the computerised main courante platform of the security ministry (MATDS) was not yet operational: the digital transition ministry put it at more than 80% built, and the MATDS director of information systems said it would be operational by mid-January 2024, once amendments were taken in.

The article states that the platform is to replace the physical registers in which main courantes are kept at police commissariats and gendarmerie brigades; at late December 2023 those registers were still the record.

At late December 2023 no commissariat or gendarmerie brigade was using the computerised main courante: the platform was over 80% built and due to be operational by mid-January 2024; no number of stations is given.

The platform is described as that of the Ministère de l'Administration Territoriale, de la Décentralisation et de la Sécurité, its director of information systems (a police commissaire principal) reporting on it to a delegation of the digital transition ministry in late December 2023; no partner, vendor or source of finance is named.
